name: CIV
label: Revelation
lede: Walter Schreifels wrote the songs, three Gorilla Biscuits played them, and a talk-show spoof the band shot itself landed on MTV's Buzz Bin and Beavis and Butt-head.

eras.title: Gorilla Biscuits under another name
eras.text: Gorilla Biscuits had broken up and Walter Schreifels was busy with the heavy records of Quicksand. He still had fast, funny, hooky songs, and he knew which friends should play them.

years.big: "I wanted to have the freedom to do new stuff and be funnier in some ways."
years.src: Wikipedia: CIV · No Echo · Riot Fest
years.h: CIV forms around the singer's name, not Gorilla Biscuits'
years.p: Singer [[Anthony Civarelli|a5d69704-924b-4128-9577-e16531503890]] and bassist [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]] come from Gorilla Biscuits, drummer [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] from [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] and [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]], with guitarist [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]]. That's Walter Schreifels on why it isn't called Gorilla Biscuits.
years.xp:
Smilios had finished college by 1994 and missed playing. "The timing was perfect," he told No Echo.

Schreifels, whose band [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] had signed to a major, had a second reason for the new name: "People who are really into hardcore have a real ownership of the group." A band that veered off the path, even slightly, could be "totally wrecked for it."

years.h: Schreifels writes the songs without joining
years.p: Walter Schreifels writes most of CIV's debut, Set Your Goals, and co-produces it with [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]] from 1994 into 1995. After Quicksand, he said, it was nice to have something that wasn't heavy.
years.xp: The people he made it with were his best friends, Schreifels told Riot Fest, "so the vibe was just really good."

eras.title: Buzz Bin
eras.text: CIV came out of the Revelation family, signed to Atlantic's Lava imprint, shot a video for Can't Wait One Minute More itself, and turned up on MTV and Beavis and Butt-head. Few bands from the NYHC matinees got that far into the mainstream.

years.big: "If I could do it over again, I would have stayed with an independent label."
years.h: CIV signs with Atlantic's Lava imprint
years.p: Arthur Smilios, on the deal with Lava, the Atlantic imprint run by Jason Flom. Some of the staff cared about the artists, he said, but the corporate climate wore on him.

years.src: Wikipedia: Set Your Goals · Revelation Records
yt: Can't Wait One Minute More on Beavis and Butt-head
years.h: Set Your Goals comes out on Revelation and Lava
years.p: Produced by Don Fury and Walter Schreifels, it reaches No. 11 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 184 on the Billboard 200. A Bay Area band later names itself [[Set Your Goals|03d8f83e-a647-4bde-968a-189c0f147783]] after it.
years.xp: Michael Barbiero mixed Set Your Goals. The singles also came out on Revelation vinyl.

q: We made the video ourselves and it got on MTV.
yt: Can't Wait One Minute More, the video
years.h: A talk-show spoof the band shot itself gets on MTV
years.p: Can't Wait One Minute More, with [[Lou Koller|f1549cac-a48c-4741-8edd-09c1016ada64]] of [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] on guest vocals, is Marcos Siega's first music video. It goes into MTV's Buzz Bin and onto Beavis and Butt-head, and reaches No. 21 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks.
years.xp:
Schreifels called it the best song-and-video pairing he'd had, and the cheapness was part of the pitch. "We were commenting on talk show culture," he said, "like Jerry Springer and that kind of thing." Choices Made got a video too.

Can't Wait One Minute More kept turning up for a decade: a Nissan commercial around 2005, What's New, Scooby-Doo?, Mega Man and Road Rash 3D.

yt: Can't Wait One Minute More live, Amsterdam, January 28, 1996
years.h: CIV lands on the Escape from L.A. soundtrack
years.p: John Carpenter's film gives CIV a soundtrack slot. More singles follow on Lava and Atlantic.

eras.title: A second album, a hiatus
eras.text: Thirteen Day Getaway arrived in 1998 with new producers, a new bassist and Schreifels no longer the main writer. It was dedicated to Warzone singer Raybeez, who died in 1997, and critics split hard. By 2000 CIV had called a halt.

years.h: Smilios steps out, Cache Tolman steps in
years.p: Arthur Smilios leaves before CIV's second album, Thirteen Day Getaway, is finished, and [[Cache Tolman|1d48168d-10f9-48f7-9cb9-622f1a0e39c1]] takes over on bass. Walter Schreifels contributes a single song this time.
years.xp: Smilios told No Echo he'd already left by the time CIV broke up, which he dates to around 1998-1999, so he doesn't know the specifics of the end.

years.p: Ray Barbieri, a fixture of the CBGB matinees, dies of complications from pneumonia. CIV dedicates Thirteen Day Getaway to him.

q: I maintain that it was a great record that was about a decade ahead of its time.
years.src: Wikipedia: Thirteen Day Getaway · No Echo
yt: Can't Wait One Minute More on MTV, 1998
years.p: Pitchfork gives CIV's second album a 1.0, Germany's Rock Hard a 7.5. Michael Barbiero, John Goodmanson and Steve Thompson produced it, and it's dedicated to Ray "Raybeez" Barbieri.
years.xp:
The Plain Dealer heard one more post-[[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] band. The San Diego Union-Tribune heard pop hooks with a punk charge. Nobody heard the same record.

Smilios, who'd left before it was done, has defended it ever since. He told No Echo it was "criticized and unappreciated."

years.p: The single from CIV's Thirteen Day Getaway comes out a month after the album.

years.h: After two albums, CIV goes on permanent hiatus
years.p: CIV announces the hiatus in 2000, after Set Your Goals and Thirteen Day Getaway.

eras.title: Goals, revisited
eras.text: The reunions came as one-offs, each tied to an occasion: a hardcore bowling-alley weekend, a Belgian festival, a New York ballroom.

years.h: The Black N Blue Bowl is CIV's first show since the hiatus
years.p: CIV plays the hardcore weekend in 2008.

years.cap: Anthony Civarelli singing with CIV at Resurrection Fest, Spain, July 2011
years.h: Groezrock in Belgium puts CIV back on a big stage

years.cap: A crowd at CIV's show at Coney Island High, New York, June 2011
years.h: CIV headlines Webster Hall on East 11th Street
years.p: CIV plays the New York ballroom on September 7, 2012.

eras.title: Sharing a bill with Shelter
eras.text: Sammy Siegler had been back in Shelter since 2018. In 2024 CIV and Shelter went out together.

yt: Can't Wait One Minute More, Bowery Ballroom, April 7, 2024
years.h: CIV tours the Northeast with Shelter, then plays the Netherlands
years.p: CIV supports [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] on a Northeast run and plays the Netherlands in November.

sources.title: Rest Assured: R.I.P. Raybeez, Nov 27 1961 – Sept 11 1997
